name: paper_gmboostcg
description: Canonical gm-boosted common-gate LNA: a common-gate input transistor (M1, source = the RF input node directly) whose gate is driven by an auxiliary inverting common-source stage (M2, gate = the same input node, drain-resistor load R1) instead of a fixed AC-ground bias -- boosting M1's effective transconductance to gm1*(1+A), where A is the auxiliary stage's gain, which loosens the classic link between noise figure and the 1/gm input-matching condition. Drain load L1 sets the output.

cited_paper.title: Gm-Boosted Common-Gate LNA and Differential Colpitts VCO/QVCO in 0.18-um CMOS
cited_paper.authors: Xiaoyong Li, Sudip Shekhar, David J. Allstot
cited_paper.venue: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits (December 2005 issue, per the hosting IEEE Denver SSCS chapter reference archive)
cited_paper.open_access: PDF hosted by an IEEE regional chapter's public reference archive; not formally verified as the publisher's official open-access copy
cited_paper.what_was_actually_read: The PDF could NOT be text-extracted by the available fetch tool (it returned raw PDF structure/image-object data, not readable text -- the schematic pages are embedded as scanned images). Confidence in this transcription therefore rests on web-search-result abstracts/summaries of the paper (which describe a transformer-coupled gm-boosted common-gate LNA, both single-ended and fully-differential variants) plus general, well-established gm-boosted-CG circuit theory, NOT on directly reading this paper's schematic.

transcription.route: Authored directly in AnalogGenie native format; validated through upstream build_connection_matrix/dfs_all_paths (execed read-only) -> token sequence -> lna/topology.py screen -> lna/to_spice.py -> ngspice.
simplifications_from_the_paper: The paper's actual auxiliary boosting stage is TRANSFORMER-COUPLED (per search-result summaries), not a plain resistor-loaded CS inverter. AnalogGenie's device vocabulary has no mutual-inductance/transformer primitive (see the same limitation noted in paper_transformerfb's provenance), so this transcription uses the simpler, textbook resistor-loaded CS auxiliary stage that implements the identical gm-boosting FEEDBACK MECHANISM (auxiliary inverting gain from the input node to M1's gate) without the transformer's specific coupling -- structurally the same boosting topology, electrically a different (simpler, non-transformer) realization of it.

transcription_confidence: MEDIUM. The gm-boosting MECHANISM (auxiliary inverting stage from the CG transistor's source/input node to its gate, replacing a fixed AC-ground bias) is HIGH confidence -- this is the defining, unambiguous feature of the entire topology family and is well documented across many independent papers, not just this one. Confidence is capped at MEDIUM specifically because this paper's own schematic was not machine-readable, so the auxiliary stage's exact realization (transformer-coupled in the source paper vs. resistor-loaded here) is a deliberate, disclosed simplification rather than a verified match to the source figure.
ambiguous_or_uncertain: Transformer coupling in the boosting path (source paper) vs. simple resistive CS stage (this transcription) -- disclosed above.
Whether the source paper's LNA is single-ended or fully differential -- search results mention both variants; this transcription is single-ended, the simpler of the two.
No component values were available (PDF not text-readable); to_spice.py's standard placeholder .param defaults were used.

validation.structural_screen: 5/5 -- all criteria pass (1 inductor / 4 devices = 25% ratio; 4 devices, the smallest/cleanest transcription in this batch, matching the minimal 2-transistor essence of the technique).
validation.ngspice_sim: clean run, op + sp(1-4GHz) + noise, zero errors. S11min=-4.17dB, S21max=-22.8dB with generic placeholder sizing.

excluded_paper_check: Independent of, and unrelated to, the Kanchetla et al. TMTT 2022 paper this pipeline is blind-reproducing. This is a 2005 paper (17 years earlier) from different authors on a general CG-LNA/VCO technique, not a GNSS receiver.
